stem: A company runs an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster with one writer and four Aurora Replicas: two large replicas and two small replicas. The team adds and removes replicas often. Each web request opens a new database connection. Monthly analytics queries must run only on the two large replicas, which have the memory that these queries need. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: must run only on the two large replicas
The team adds and removes replicas often

options.text: Connect the read-only queries to the reader endpoint of the cluster, and keep the writes on the cluster endpoint.
options.why: The reader endpoint [balances connections to available Aurora Replicas](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-reader-endpoint-balances-connections-not-queries), the small ones included, so analytics queries also land on the small replicas.
options.misconception: believes that the reader endpoint can be limited to some of the replicas

options.text: Create a custom endpoint that contains the two large replicas, and connect the read-only queries to the custom endpoint.
options.why: A custom endpoint represents [a set of DB instances that you choose](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-custom-endpoint-set-of-chosen-instances), so the analytics queries reach the two large replicas and no other instance.

options.text: Connect all queries of the application, writes included, to the reader endpoint, so that every replica shares the work.
options.why: The cluster endpoint is [the only one that can perform write operations](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-cluster-endpoint-only-one-for-writes), so writes sent to the reader endpoint fail on the replicas.

options.text: Store the instance endpoint of each replica in the application settings, and choose one endpoint in the code for each query.
options.why: It works, but the team must [hardcode all the hostnames](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-endpoint-abstracts-connections-no-hardcode) and keep them current when replicas change.

explanation: The analytics queries need a chosen group of replicas. A custom endpoint represents [a set of DB instances that you choose](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-custom-endpoint-set-of-chosen-instances), and you can define one for [instances that use a particular AWS instance class](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-custom-endpoint-use-different-instance-classes-reporting). Aurora balances connections among the members, so the team names the endpoint once and changes no code when other replicas come and go.
takeaway: Reads on chosen instances, such as large ones for analytics: a custom endpoint.
twin: If the stem said "Read-only queries from the web application must be spread across all the replicas" instead: the reader endpoint, because it gives [connection-balancing among all the Aurora Replicas](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-reader-endpoint-balances-replicas).
say: A custom endpoint is a named group of instances, so the analytics queries reach only the two large replicas.
